description: Append-only progress/log record for a run. Committed immediately so a reader on a different thread/connection can observe it (WAL mode, ADR-006).
signature: def append_run_event(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, *, stage: str, level: str, message: str, progress: float | None = None) -> int
docstring:
Append one progress/log event.

Args:
    conn: An open connection (the pipeline's own connection, per ADR-006's 'one connection per thread' rule).
    run_id: The run this event belongs to.
    stage: Pipeline stage name, e.g. 'acquisition', 'enrichment', 'analysis'.
    level: One of 'debug', 'info', 'warning', 'error'.
    message: Human-readable, English-language event text.
    progress: Fractional completion in [0.0, 1.0], or None.

Returns:
    The generated event_id (monotonically increasing per database).

Raises:
    StorageError: If run_id does not exist, level is invalid, or progress is outside [0.0, 1.0].
postconditions: The row is committed to disk before the function returns (no batching/deferred commit), so a concurrent reader immediately sees it under WAL
event_id values are strictly increasing across the whole database, not just per run

edge_cases.expected_behavior: accepted -- storage does not enforce non-empty messages; an empty message is a caller-quality issue, not a storage-layer invariant

edge_cases.input: Called concurrently from two different EventSink instances writing to the same run_id via separate connections
edge_cases.expected_behavior: both succeed with distinct, correctly ordered event_ids; SQLite's own locking under WAL serializes the two writers

unit_tests.name: test_append_and_read_back
unit_tests.description: An appended event is immediately visible via read_run_events.
unit_tests.expected: read_run_events returns exactly one matching RunEvent

unit_tests.name: test_unknown_run_id_raises
unit_tests.description: Appending to a nonexistent run_id raises StorageError.
